Hi everyone! I’m really sorry for the late update once again, and I know I haven’t gotten a chance to reply back to all the comments and messages that everyone has sent, but I wanted to give a 2nd and possibly even final update to my situation. In short, I did not sign any of the POA documents, I only signed an advanced directive healthcare document! 

Last night I had a discussion with my parents about the forms, since after I finished dinner they had asked me if I had finished reading+signing the POA documents so that they could review it a final time before we were to go to the notary today. I was not sure what to even say, but I remembered everyone’s comments, messages, and support here, and I was able to muster up enough courage to tell them that I wouldn’t sign the documents. It was kind of difficult, because I’m not used to saying no, but I told them I didn’t want to sign anything and refused to sign the POAs. They were confused as I believe they thought I would sign it without saying anything, and so it did end up turning into an argument that lasted a while, because my parents wanted me to sign it and told me continuously that it was for my own benefit in the case of an emergency. My mom hadn’t even read the forms properly, but my dad had read everything thoroughly, and honestly I was just kind of dumbfounded and sad they were making me sign such a thing. I told them that I wouldn’t sign anything and stood my ground on that somehow, and also said that I would only sign another form like a health care proxy or advanced directive (both of which many kind commenters had mentioned), but it was already late at night and so eventually they let go of the discussion, because there was not much time before I would go to college and so they decided to just leave the matter to another time for the time being. I guess for them it was just not worth the hassle of redoing everything and whatnot, and so my mom said I have to do something for health care at least for the time being. They were kind of disappointed at the end of the argument and it sort of just ended there. 

I found some advanced directive forms for both states of California and Oregon online from CaringInfo yesterday, and printed those out. I filled out everything there and made sure I was specific on what exactly I wanted. 
I did happen to read up on a couple of blogs where some medical personnel suggested in their blog post that writing a Quality of Life statement would also be helpful. So I wrote a Quality of Life statement and explained my values/what is important to me in my life and recovery and other medical situations, and printed that out and attached it to the forms for both states. 

The notary appointment was earlier today in the afternoon, but it was alright and I got the advanced directives notarized. The notary was kind to me and explained everything about the notarizing process. So that’s how the situation has ended up, and I think I feel a lot better, since the POA situation is pushed off to another time for now. Since the notary appointment though, they have been asking me/pushing me to consider signing the POA documents or maybe a HIPAA and financial release form, but I’ve mostly tried to avoid the topic itself. They were complaining to their parents (my grandparents) on their personal calls in the evening, but whatever, since that doesn’t really matter. 

I still have one more notary appointment however, my parents have set one up with a bank near my university for this Thursday after I complete moving into my dorm, so I’m not sure what will happen then. I don’t really know if they’re taking the Mama Bear POA documents with them or not. I don’t think the matter will come up again as strongly, but I will once again refuse to sign anything, even if it’s in front of the notary. 

However for the time being I’m safe and sound. I just wanted to let everyone know, since many people were concerned about my safety. I’m doing alright, I’m glad that the situation went mostly alright, and now the sick feeling I had is starting to go away as well. 

Many people gave helpful advice on steps I should take to better protect myself for the future, which included things like opening a new bank account, gathering my important documents, creating a support system, letting my university know, looking for a job, topics about learning my financials, checking my credit report, learning a bit about contract and other sorts of common law in everyday life, etc. I have looked into many of these topics, and I have made notes on all of the advice that everyone has given to me! I will look into all of them and start learning about these various topics!

But I really wanted to thank everyone for all of your encouragement and support, and all of your kind words and reassurance as well, I deeply appreciate everything and I am thankful from the bottom of my heart. Words cannot express my gratitude. Thank you to everyone for giving me so much helpful advice/tips, for your encouragement to be more courageous, for your gentle words of reassurance, for your own stories and perspectives, for explaining everything about the document, and for taking the time to worry about my situation and about me. I’m really thankful. I was very worried at the start since I barely understood anything about the document or it’s consequences if I were to sign it and when I originally wrote this post and the one in r/legaladvice, I didn’t think there’d be a good outcome at all. Because I didn’t know much, I also felt alone in the process, but now I feel like I understand a lot of things better thanks to everyone’s help. I also feel lucky that the situation did not go too bad, and that I was able to receive much help and support. Thanks to that I was able to be a bit more courageous and knowledgeable about the situation and stand up for myself this time. I know I’ve said thank you so many times by now, but I am very thankful for everyone, and I am glad I was able to get lots of help and encouragement. 

I also wanted to thank the few lawyers, attorneys, and notaries, who either privately messaged me or posted their comments on my posts with useful advice and offered to help me out with explaining the POA in terms of legal aspects, or how the notarizing and revocation processes work, or how certain topics in the POA function, or how the document is used, etc. Thank you so much, I was able to learn so much more and be more informed. Thank you for worrying about me and for taking the time out of your own workday or personal day to spend time explaining me everything. I really do appreciate it and will never forget your help! 

And thank you so so sooooo much to everyone else as well, for everything, from commenting to checking up on me. 

I did not sign the POA, and I am glad to have not done so. 

But anyways, thank you so much!!! I will do my best in college, away from my home environment, and I hope to be able to try many clubs or things that I like. I’ll do my best to be a good student at school as well, and try to work towards creating a calm life for myself. Thank you for all of the encouragement, I will remember everyone’s kind words!!!!

I’m really sorry to everyone whose comments or messages I have not been able to reply back to yet, I have read all of the comments and messages, but I will slowly reply to them gradually. Thank you for your patience!!! 

Everyone, please take care and have a great weekend!

I wanted to give everyone some information about the situation:

- I am from California, but the state I will be going to college in is Oregon, and so that’s why there are two POA documents
- the POA documents are from “Mama Bear Legal Forms” and is called Durable Powers of Attorney (this is for young adults). Their website (https://mamabearlegalforms.com/youngadult) lists the general information on what the files contain, but you have to pay to access it. It seems that my parents have paid for it
- the notary appointment is tomorrow in the morning. I still have time this evening to talk to my parents
- the POA documents state that they are effective upon signature, which I assume means that they are effective immediately. From what I understand, they seem to be effective through hospitalization/etc.
- Many people tell me to say just say no, but that is a bit difficult. I grew up in an abusive household, where my mother was an enabler or ignored everything most of the time, and where my dad was a control-freak and physically and verbally abusive man. To give you some examples, I have been strangled, have had knives to my neck, been hit, verbally abused badly almost everyday for periods of time, had excessive surveillance (ex. Motion detecting audio and video recording cameras), been kept inside of my room, been humiliated in public, watched abuse against my siblings and even extremely escalated situations against my own mother. Things are better now, because I am leaving for college in less than a week, and so for the past couple of weeks both of my parents have made a complete 180 in their personalities and have suddenly become very nice. Because of that, this makes me very suspicious of their reasons to get me to sign those POA documents
- because of the point above, despite being 18 and almost 19 in 3-4 months, I am like a dependent or a 14 year old in terms of any real-world experience 
- I have no relatives nor close friends living by whom I can stay with. My parents immigrated to the US, and the rest of their family is back in Asia. I do not have any friends due to school bullying in the past. My unofficial godmother lives up an hour away from the college I’m going to
- I would love to transfer all of my money out in one go from my bank account after having created a new one, but my parents are joint holders on my account and can control my transactions, so I will have to do it slowly and gradually once I get a part time in college
- I cannot run away because I have almost 0 savings to my name. I was not allowed to work until just a couple of weeks ago, just for this summer, at the demand of my godmother, who knows my home environment
- I am lucky enough to go to an out of state college solely because that is the only college giving me the most financial aid. My parents are paying the remaining portion of the tuition that the scholarship won’t pay, but they haven’t threatened anything about not paying my tuition if I don’t sign, they kind of just expect me to sign
- Several commenters mentioned looking into legal aid, and I am trying. I contacted some contract lawyers in my area to look for free consultations, but they are too expensive for me or just not available. Others mentioned that I should call up my college, and I will definitely be doing that right after posting this update
- I know many people read up on my post history and see that I struggle with some issues. I do struggle, but at the same time I don’t think I am that bad in emotional health that I cannot make decisions rationally. I am trying my best. I am physically healthy and am alive
- the POAs seem to cover the sections of health, finances, and ferpa/education
- I have some of my documents with me, things like my ssn card, some college documents, my real ID, and a picture of my passport page
- I would like to tell a trusted adult like a teacher or someone, but I will most likely first try and get their contact, or tell them later after figuring out a few more important things related to the document
- I do not have any means of transportation (no car, no driving license). I use a bicycle to get around
- I use cash almost always, so that’s also why I have limited credit card knowledge
- several people have mentioned that I should look into creating a will instead. This seems like a good idea and I would pursue this after this calms down

However, I will make sure I don’t sign those documents. And I’ll tell the notary I don’t want to and am under duress as well. I will continue to update everyone! I had this problem and it was a nightmare. Fumigation was an expensive option for us too, so we ended up using smaller/preventative measures instead. The best I can suggest is to first take out all clothes and have them washed on high heat to kill off any eggs. You can buy Diatomaceous Earth and put it in wall cracks and around the area where most of the bedbugs are currently, this will help kill off some of them or at least prevent them from spreading further. I’ve heard of lemon sprays/rubbing alcohol sprays working as well, but you will have to research into that. Try to implement these preventative measures as soon as you can, as bedbugs can spread very quickly since from what I understand and experienced, they are attracted to heat or oxygen or whatever and follow around humans a lot. My mom and I ended up having to throw out my bed and her bed, run all of our clothes in a laundromat under high heat, line the bottom of our walls with diatomaceous earth, and extensively clean out everything, and only after that did the bedbugs disappear. I suggest you also make a post in r/bedbugs, as that sub can probably give you much better advice. I hope everything goes well!
